user.title: Cozy Control
user.description: Choose where the outdoor temperature comes from and which thermostat to control. You can change the temperature table, off range and seasons afterwards in the integration's settings.

data.weather_entity: Outdoor temperature source (weather entity or temperature sensor)
data.update_interval: How often to check and update (minutes)

init.description: Pick a section to edit. Choose Save when you are done.

general.title: Source, interval and units
general.description: Temperatures here are shown in {unit}. You can pick several outdoor sources (weather entities or temperature sensors, such as your own outdoor sensor). With more than one, the next page sets how much each counts.

data.update_interval: How often to check and update (minutes)
data.range_width: Width of the heat/cool range (when both are allowed)

data_description.unit: 'Follow Home Assistant' uses your Home Assistant unit system. Stored values are converted automatically, so changing this never changes the real temperatures.
data_description.range_width: Used on thermostats with a heat/cool range mode: the thermostat heats below the target minus half this width and cools above the target plus half.
data_description.interpolate: On: 25 outside gives a value between the 20 and 30 rows. Off: the row at or below the outdoor temperature is used.

setpoints.title: Temperature table
setpoints.description:
One pair per line as 'outdoor: indoor' in {unit}. The thermostat target follows this table based on the outdoor temperature. Example: "{example}" means {example_inside} inside when it is {example_outside} outside.

{error}

bedtime.title: Bedtime temperatures
bedtime.description:
Between the start and end time every day, the thermostat follows this table instead of the main one. Type times like {time_example}; the window may cross midnight. One pair per line as 'outdoor: indoor' in {unit}. Example: "{example}" means {example_inside} inside when it is {example_outside} outside.

{error}

off_range.title: Turn off in mild weather
off_range.description: When the outdoor temperature is between these values (in {unit}), the thermostat is turned off. The values are kept when you switch this off, so you can switch it back on later.

data.off_enabled: Turn the thermostat off in mild weather

heat_cool.title: Heating and cooling
heat_cool.description: Switch heating and cooling on or off here. Turn both off and the thermostat is switched off. This applies on top of the date ranges, so a mode runs only when it is on here and today is not inside its disabled dates.

seasons.title: Disable heating or cooling on dates
seasons.description:
One range per line as 'MM-DD to MM-DD'. They repeat every year and may cross New Year (for example '11-01 to 02-28'). Switching a list off keeps its dates, so you can switch it back on later.

{error}

windows.title: Windows and morning briefing
windows.description:
Used by the morning briefing and the windows switch. A day whose high is between Pleasant from and Pleasant up to is a good day to open windows. Temperatures are in {unit}.

{error}

data.use_forecast: Use today's forecast high and low
data.win_resume: After a Yes, resume the program at
data.win_max_hours: Always resume the program after at most (hours, 0 for never)
data.brief_dates_enabled: Only give the briefing on these dates

data_description.use_forecast: Needs a weather entity as the source. With a plain temperature sensor the current temperature is used.
data_description.win_max_hours: A safety net so the house does not stay off if the windows are forgotten open.
data_description.brief_dates: One range per line as MM-DD to MM-DD, for example spring and autumn. They repeat every year.

presence.title: Phones and presence
presence.description: Away mode uses a second temperature table while nobody is home. Pick the phones (device trackers from the Home Assistant app) or people to watch. The house counts as home if any of them is inside the radius around your Home Assistant home location, and as away only when all of them have been outside it for the delay. If no phone has a usable reading, the house counts as home. Each phone also gets its own switch so you can turn its location on or off at any time.

data.presence_max_accuracy: Ignore GPS readings less accurate than

data_description.presence_radius: Distance from your Home Assistant home location that counts as home. Pick something larger than your typical GPS error to avoid false 'away' readings.
data_description.presence_delay: Everyone must stay away for this long before the Away table is used. Coming home takes effect immediately.
data_description.presence_max_accuracy: Phones sometimes report a rough position. Readings less accurate than this are ignored instead of being trusted.

away_temps.title: Away temperatures
away_temps.description:
While nobody is home the thermostat follows this table instead of the main one (and instead of the bedtime table). One pair per line as 'outdoor: indoor' in {unit}. Example: "{example}" means {example_inside} inside when it is {example_outside} outside.

{error}

contacts.title: Window and door sensors
contacts.description: While any of the sensors you pick reports open, the thermostat is turned off. When all of them are closed again, it goes back to following your rules and can turn the heating or cooling back on. Window, door, opening and garage door sensors are offered. A sensor that is unavailable is ignored, so a dead battery never holds the thermostat off by itself, but a sensor stuck on 'open' would.

data.contacts_enabled: Turn the thermostat off while a window or door is open
data.contact_delay: Wait before turning the thermostat off

data_description.contact_delay: The window or door must stay open this long first, so quickly letting the dog out does not switch the heating off. Closing takes effect within seconds.

safety.title: Safety temperatures
safety.description: A last line of defence that looks only at the temperature inside the house and ignores the outdoor weather. If the indoor temperature reaches the hot limit, cooling starts; if it falls to the cold limit, heating starts. This beats every other setting: the temperature table, Away mode, open windows and doors, the no-heating and no-cooling dates, the heating/cooling switches and the pause switch. Once triggered it keeps going until the house has recovered by {margin} {unit}. Temperatures are in {unit}. The thermostat's own limits still apply (Nest allows heating from about 7 °C and cooling up to about 35 °C).

data.safety_cold: Heat if the house drops to

data_description.safety_sensors: The thermostat's own reading is always used. Add room sensors (such as Nest temperature sensors) and the hottest and coldest reading of all of them is checked.

indoor.title: Indoor temperature sensors
indoor.description:
By default the thermostat steers by its own temperature reading. Pick other sensors here and the rules aim at the average of those instead. The thermostat's own reading is only used if you add the thermostat to the list, so leave it out to ignore it. Leave the list empty to use only the thermostat.

The next page lets you add time windows that use different sensors, such as the crib sensor at night.

The thermostat is asked for a slightly different target so that your sensors' average reaches the temperature you actually want.

data.indoor_max_offset: Largest shift allowed to the thermostat's target

data_description.indoor_sources: Temperature sensors, and thermostats (their own reading).
data_description.indoor_max_offset: A sensor far from the thermostat can read very differently. This caps how far the target can be moved so a faulty sensor cannot cause extreme settings. Shown in {unit}.

indoor_weights.title: How much each sensor counts
indoor_weights.description: A bigger number gives a sensor more influence on the average. 0 ignores it, and the same weight for all of them gives a plain average.

indoor_windows.title: Indoor sensors by time of day

menu_options.indoor_window_pick: Change or remove a time window

indoor_window_add.title: Add a time window
indoor_window_add.description: The sensors you pick are used between these times every day. A window may cross midnight.

indoor_window_edit.title: Change a time window
indoor_window_edit.description: The sensors you pick are used between these times every day. A window may cross midnight.

outdoor_weights.title: How much each outdoor source counts
outdoor_weights.description: A bigger number gives a source more influence on the average. 0 ignores it, and the same weight for all of them gives a plain average. A source that is unavailable is skipped and the others share its weight.

error.invalid_table: The table could not be read. Check each line looks like '20: 21' and temperatures are realistic.
error.off_range_incomplete: Fill in both values, or leave both empty.
error.off_range_needed: Enter both temperatures, or switch this off.
error.invalid_time: A time could not be read. Use a time like 20:00 or 8:00 PM.
error.bedtime_same_time: Bedtime must start and end at different times.
error.invalid_dates: A date range could not be read. Use 'MM-DD to MM-DD'.
error.window_order: The temperatures must go in order: cold, pleasant from, pleasant up to, hot.
error.invalid_windows_input: Something could not be read. Check the time (like 6:00 PM) and the dates (like 03-15 to 05-31).
error.safety_order: The hot limit must be at least 8 °C (14 °F) above the cold limit.
error.indoor_same_time: A time window cannot start and end at the same time.
error.indoor_window_needs_sensor: Pick at least one sensor for the window.
error.outdoor_needs_source: Pick at least one outdoor temperature source.

state.door_or_window_open: Off: a window or door is open

morning_briefing.name: Morning briefing
morning_briefing.description: Works out today's advice about the windows and the thermostat, and asks a question when one helps. It also ends any windows-open period so the day starts normally. Returns the message, and can send it to a speaker.

notify_entity.name: Speak on
notify_entity.description: A notify entity that reads the message aloud, such as an Alexa Devices Announce entity.

answer.name: Answer the question
answer.description: Answers the question from the last morning briefing with yes or no.

windows_opened.name: Windows opened
windows_opened.description: Marks the windows as open and switches the thermostat off until the windows are marked closed, or until the time or hours given, or the safety limit in the settings.

hours.name: Resume after
hours.description: Resume the program after this many hours.

until.name: Resume at
until.description: Resume the program at this time of day.

windows_closed.name: Windows closed
windows_closed.description: Marks the windows as closed. The thermostat follows the rules again.

feel.name: I'm cold or warm
feel.description: Makes the house warmer or cooler now, and remembers it: the temperature table in use (normal, bedtime or away) is changed at today's outdoor temperature. Returns a message saying what changed.

feeling.name: Feeling
feeling.description: Cold makes it warmer, warm makes it cooler.

step.name: Change by
step.description: How much warmer or cooler, in the unit shown in the settings. Without it: 0.5 °C (1 °F).

undo_feel.name: Undo comfort change
undo_feel.description: Puts the temperature table back as it was before the last "I'm cold" or "I'm warm". Returns a message saying what changed.
